$comment: Cases from the review of the interpolation judgement, judged by both editors alike: markup only when a hole's whole result is markup, + chains inside templates, the scope of names, Streamlord's own helpers and kotlinx.html output, quick fixes that would change the page, and how holes are named. A case may give `constants`, the workspace's const val names.

cases.name: an if with one HTML branch and a String branch is not markup
cases.source:
fun f(admin: Boolean, q: String) = "

${if (admin) "admin" else q}

"

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${if (admin) "admin" els…} into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Trusted fun f(admin: Boolean, q: String) = "

${Trusted(if (admin) "admin" else q)}

"

cases.name: the workspace constant is silent where the file declares nothing else of its name
a lambda parameter of interpolate is not the String it shadows
cases.source:
fun f(q: String) = listOf(1, 2).map { q -> interpolate("""

""", q) }

issues.message: interpolate throws here unless q is a number or a boolean: it lands in data-text, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Put the value in a signal and reference it from the expression, or write the signal's name in the markup yourself.

cases.name: a Streamlord helper in a Datastar expression is the author's code
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.signal
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.post

fun f() = """<button data-on:click="${post("/x")}" data-text="${signal("running")} ? 'Stop' : 'Go'"></button>"""

cases.name: a Streamlord helper in a DSL call is the author's code
a helper of that name from elsewhere is not Streamlord's

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${signal("running")} into data-text, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path. Text from outside becomes code there, even inside quotes. Put the value in a signal, or in an attribute of its own read with el.dataset; only a number or a boolean is safe to write in.
